facts.statement: A German amateur paleontologist named Kurt Wiedenroth discovered the skeleton of Thaumatodracon in 1969 along the coast of Dorset in the UK.
facts.quote: In early 1969, German amateur paleontologist Kurt Wiedenroth at the coast of Dorset between Lyme Regis and Charmouth discovered a plesiosaur skeleton.

facts.statement: The species Thaumatodracon wiedenrothi was formally named and described by Adam Smith and Ricardo Araújo in 2017.
facts.quote: In 2017, the type species Thaumatodracon wiedenrothi was named and described by Smith and Araùjo.

facts.statement: The specific name wiedenrothi was chosen to honor the fossil's discoverer, Kurt Wiedenroth.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Wiedenroth as discoverer.

facts.statement: Thaumatodracon lived during the Early Jurassic period in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Thaumatodracon is a genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosaur from the early Jurassic found in the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: Thaumatodracon is classified as a rhomaleosaurid pliosaur.
facts.quote: Thaumatodracon is a genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosaur from the early Jurassic found in the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Thaumatodracon was found in the Black Ven Mudstone Member of the Charmouth Mudstone Formation from the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, NLMH 106.058, originated from the Black Ven Mudstone Member of the Charmouth Mudstone Formation dating from the Sinemurian.

facts.statement: Thaumatodracon lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)
